text:
maria: FYI I'm seeing a persistent regional hit-rate gap for prefix/KV cache between us-east and eu-west starting ~03:00 UTC yesterday. us-east hit ~72% vs eu-west ~39% on the same model and workload.
raj: rough magnitude of QPS?
maria: ~8k global QPS, ~2.1k in eu-west. The misses in eu-west are all short prefixes (<= 32 tokens).
eli: are keys canonicalized? header differences, shard ids, or user-agent could produce different keys.
maria: good call — I dumped sample keys and found duplicates caused by minor metadata differences. Example: `prefix:v1|tokhash:abc123|ua:chrome` vs `prefix:v1|tokhash:abc123|ua:curl` — UA was included in key by older codepath.
szymon: ohhh. That'll increase cardinality and reduce reuse — especially in low-traffic regions.
maria: Also saw replication lag spikes in eu-west at the same times (replication queue depth ~1800). Combined effect = priming never catches up.
raj: can you paste the profiling snippet for kernel / batching we saw that correlates with the gap?
maria: pasted below — it's the per-kernel time series around the miss window. Note the kernel selector flips to the long-seq kernel at 512 token budget which increases per-request tail latency and effectively reduces throughput, so fewer warm prefixes get inserted.
```
# profiler snippet (trimmed)
2026-03-17T02:58:12Z kernel_selector: light_attn_v2 (seq<=256) latency p95=42ms
2026-03-17T02:58:44Z kernel_selector: long_attn_opt (seq>256) latency p95=98ms
2026-03-17T03:01:03Z batcher: avg_batch_size=4 -> dropped to 2 during spike
```

eli: so two interacting problems: bad keying multiplicity + kernel-induced throughput drop -> batches shrink -> fewer cache inserts -> cold region.
raj: what about cache eviction churn? any evidence of repeated evicts?
maria: yes, eviction rate doubled in eu-west during gap window. From logs: `evict_ops/s 120 -> 240`. Also saw a pattern of repeated inserts for same normalized prefix but different key variants.
szymon: suggested fixes: (1) strip UA/volatile metadata from cache key at generation time, (2) add key normalization layer in routing edge, (3) temporarily increase replication priority for prefix cache objects to reduce lag, and (4) tweak kernel selection thresholds so short prefixes don't get pushed into long-seq path.
eli: agree. Also propose small canary: normalize keys + single-region prewarm for eu-west traffic spikes (pre-warm top 2k prefixes for 10m windows).
raj: are there risks? normalization could cause collisions if we drop important distinguishing fields.
maria: validated sample: we only need to drop UA and trace-id. user_id, model_ver, and prefix hash must remain. No collisions in our 24h sample.
ops-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-1642 "eu-west prefix cache hit-rate gap" (severity: low, owner: @maria).
deploy-bot: Canary rollout of key-normalization patch started in us-east (1/3 hosts) at 03:30 UTC.
maria: rollout logs: us-east canary shows hit-rate up to 88% after normalization and eviction rate down ~45% within 5m.
raj: good. schedule for eu-west rollout? Also need replication tuning.
maria: proposing: (a) eu-west rollout in 15m, (b) temporarily increase replication bandwidth for prefix cache (config: `replication.window_priority=prefix_cache,window=600s,weight=2`), (c) adjust kernel threshold from 256->384 for 30m as a safety check.
szymon: kernel threshold tweak could raise memory / KV pressure — we'll monitor OOM and latency p99. Add quick alarm if KV cache insert rate drops >30% after change.
eli: digging into batching heuristics — when batcher size dropped from 4->2 we lost amortized kernel performance. Maybe add burst-batching: hold 10ms to fill batches when latency budget allows.
raj: agree, but we must gate by SLO. Add experiment flag `batcher.burst_hold_ms=10` for non-SLO-critical routes.
maria: action items: 
- maria: roll key-normalization EU canary and enable replication priority (03:35 UTC)
- raj: add batcher burst hold experiment + monitor (03:45 UTC)
- szymon: add eviction and OOM alarms for kernel-threshold tweak (03:40 UTC)
- eli: run offline validation for key-normalization collisions on 72h sample (03:50 UTC)

maria: final note — this was subtle: a tiny metadata field increased key space enough that low-traffic region combined with a kernel throughput cliff made warmup ineffective. Fixing keying + reducing replication lag should resolve majority of the delta.
eli: :thumbsup:
raj: +1, thanks for the triage.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-1642 updated: status=in_progress.
maria: I'll post a short postmortem if the rollout stabilizes.
